name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean and incumbent advantage strongly favor Republicans
Fuller benefits from $2.8 million in outside support versus minimal opposition spending
Harris's $8.4 million fundraising edge is offset by only $59,000 in remaining cash
Prediction markets price roughly a 95% Republican win probability
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Fuller's incumbency, and heavy outside support on his side outweigh Harris's large fundraising haul, much of which is already spent. With no public polls or expert ratings, fundamentals and market pricing both point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or unexpected polling showing a much tighter race would be the main signal that this contest is narrowing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 14th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 19 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Clay Fuller is seeking another term and enters the general election backed by about $2.8 million in outside support, with little outside money opposing him. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and market pricing, both of which favor Republicans heavily.

Democratic challenger Shawn Harris has raised $8.4 million, far outstripping Fuller's $2.2 million, but reports only $59,000 in cash on hand after heavy spending, and outside groups have put nearly $450,000 into opposing him. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 4% chance of an upset. The forecast expects Fuller to win by roughly 16 to 17 points, with wide uncertainty given the absence of polling.
